title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The On-Call Room. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The On-Call Room
options.lineage: The hospital after midnight: the resident's on-call room, one lamp, a pager on the nightstand, and the story an attending finally tells at the end of a shift
options.thesis: The show is the conversation that happens in the on-call room after midnight, when the senior doctor tells you how they really got here.
options.viewport: A dark navy room with one warm lamp pool at left holding the show's name and a single line; at right a hand-sized pager reads WHAT BRINGS YOU IN in amber dot-matrix and blinks once; the follow links wait on the nightstand shelf below, nothing crowding anything.
options.risk: Dark plus amber slides into the generic neon dashboard if the light is not warm and the layout is not roomy; every page must stay a quiet room, not a control panel.

options.label: Seven-Segment Night Clock
options.lineage: bedside clocks, scoreboards, gas totems: one eight-cell mask where unlit segments are designed too
options.thesis: Every number on the site, episode count, event date, clock, is a lit segment mask on matte black.
options.viewport: Four giant red digits hang in the dark reading the launch date; the show name sits small beneath in grotesk; follow links are tiny lit segments.
options.risk: Prose cannot live in a segment mask, so the identity thins out past the hero.
options.case: Fuses as a detail, not a world: it loses product clarity as the whole identity but can serve the pager readout inside the assigned room.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm
options.lineage: hand-processed film strips with scratches, uneven chemistry and light leaks
options.thesis: Episodes are frames on one strip; the live one floods orange through its perforations.
options.viewport: A strip of frames runs horizontally across a gray field; one frame blooms orange and carries the title; sprocket margins hold the edge codes.
options.risk: Grain and leaks read as decoration unless each artifact is tied to a real episode event.
options.case: Fuses poorly on audience identification: film emulsion is a cinephile's world, not a med student's, and its wear textures fight the cozy brief.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: a monofrequency amber half sun doubled by a mirrored ceiling over a hazy hall
options.thesis: One amber hall; every visitor's silhouette doubled in the ceiling mirror.
options.viewport: A vast horizontal band of amber haze with a half sun completing itself at the far wall; the show name sits low on the horizon line in black grotesk.
options.risk: A single duotone flattens photos, bios and events into one undifferentiated glow.
options.case: Shares the amber warmth but loses both axes: an art-hall scene says nothing about medicine or about a podcast.

canonCard.label: The podcast site standard
canonCard.thesis: What podcast sites ship, executed impeccably: cover art, follow buttons, episode cards.
canonCard.viewport: Cover art left, title and two follow buttons right, the latest episodes as a card grid below, team headshots in a row.
